profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is tagged with the operator name CenturyLink, the legacy brand of the telecommunications company now operating as Lumen Technologies, which formally renamed itself in September 2020. Its coordinates fall in the Old Fourth Ward area of Atlanta, Fulton County, Georgia, near Currier Street NE, but this registry could not confidently match it to a specific street address: an area aggregator listing for Atlanta found six genuine, currently Lumen-branded facilities across the metro (4311 Best Road, 6855 Crescent Drive, 874 DeKalb Avenue, 953 Donnelly Avenue SW, 345 Courtland Street NE, and 180 Peachtree Street NW) and no facility listed under the older CenturyLink name at all, but none of the six could be matched to this record's own coordinates with any confidence. Rather than guess which, if any, of the six this record represents, this entry documents the ambiguity honestly and leaves the specific building unidentified. Atlanta's 56 Marietta Street and adjacent downtown carrier-hotel buildings have long served as major regional telecom interconnection points, and CenturyLink/Lumen's Atlanta presence, inherited through a long chain of legacy mergers (US West, Qwest, Embarq, and others absorbed into what became CenturyLink before the 2020 Lumen rebrand), likely includes both purpose-built colocation space and older central-office infrastructure; no evidence located this session distinguishes which category this specific record falls into. Georgia is one of the 20 states included in Lumens 2022 divestiture of its legacy CenturyLink local telephone operations to Brightspeed, a new company formed by investment firm Apollo Global Management for 7.5 billion dollars plus 1.4 billion dollars in assumed debt in a deal that closed October 3, 2022. If this Atlanta area building remains an active telecom facility, it may now operate under the Brightspeed name rather than CenturyLink, though this registry has not found a source confirming that transfer for this specific building among the six candidate Lumen addresses identified in the metro area and does not assert it.

profile.research_note: CenturyLink is the pre-September 2020 brand name of the company now operating as Lumen Technologies (see the Lumen Technologies operator record in this registry, uid 7aa4bd52, CIK 0000018926, ticker LUMN). CenturyLink announced its rebrand to Lumen on September 15, 2020. This record is retained separately per this registry's no-deletion policy and cross-linked via duplicate_of rather than merged, so facilities still tagged under the legacy CenturyLink name remain traceable.

reading:
CenturyLink is a name that no longer belongs to a company. It was the brand the Louisiana based telephone holding company used from 2009 until 15 September 2020, when it renamed itself Lumen Technologies. Lumen is the entity that files with the SEC and owns the network, and this registry holds a separate and fuller record under that name. The CenturyLink record is kept because facility data seeded from public mapping still carries the old operator string, and deleting it would quietly detach those buildings from the registry's history rather than resolve them.

The four buildings attached to this record deserve scepticism as data centres. Each was picked up from OpenStreetMap ways carrying the tag telecom=data_center and the operator string CenturyLink, and in three of the four cases there is no address, no building type beyond a generic one and no supporting evidence that the structure holds a data hall. The Oregon row is the most legible. It sits at 740 State Street in downtown Salem, a two storey building that until recently housed a CenturyLink retail store, on a site long associated with the local telephone exchange rather than with wholesale computing. The Missouri row falls in the town of Hamilton in Caldwell County, a community of a few thousand people, where the plausible telecom building is a small central office serving the surrounding rural exchanges. The Nevada row falls on the east side of Las Vegas, in territory served historically by Central Telephone Company rather than by a Bell operating company. The Georgia row falls in downtown Atlanta with no address tags at all.

This pattern matters more than any one building. A telephone exchange and a data centre share a family resemblance, both being windowless, air conditioned, generator backed rooms full of equipment, and mappers reach for telecom=data_center because it is the closest tag available. Aggregating those tags without review inflates facility counts and, worse, invites capacity estimates for buildings that have never sold a rack. None of the four rows here has a published critical IT load, a utility service size, a generator rating or any on site generation, and the correct reading is that none of them has been shown to be a commercial data centre at all.

The corporate history behind the label has also moved on twice since the tags were written. On 3 October 2022 Lumen closed the sale of its incumbent local exchange business in twenty states to Brightspeed, an Apollo backed carrier, for 7.5 billion dollars plus the assumption of 1.4 billion dollars of debt, transferring about 1.2 million broadband subscribers and keeping incumbent operations in sixteen other states. Then in 2025 Lumen agreed to sell its consumer fibre to the home business, marketed as Quantum Fiber, to AT and T for 5.75 billion dollars, a transaction Lumen has since reported as complete. Between them those two deals mean that a copper or fibre building tagged CenturyLink may now be owned by Brightspeed, by AT and T or by Lumen depending on which state it stands in and what function it serves, and the map tag will not tell you which.

The genuine infrastructure of the company under its current name is substantial and is documented in the Lumen record, including the long haul fibre network it inherited by absorbing Level 3 Communications in 2017. Level 3 was headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, and after the acquisition CenturyLink was named that city's largest employer with roughly 2,360 people at the former Level 3 campus, which is a better illustration of what this company actually is than any of the four buildings filed here.
